entries.subject: Selected source model
entries.finding: Published primary-component ellipsoid combining occultation and light-curve constraints. Its full axes differ from the two-dimensional occultation limb and from the unresolved binary system's radiometric diameter. Full approximation dimensions: 127 × 117 × 98 km. Synchronous spin-axis approximation using the same 2024 orbital pole as Menoetius; arbitrary display meridian. A physical mutual-event phase is not claimed. The grid marks unmapped terrain. Source: [Buie et al. (2015), The Astronomical Journal 149, 113; existing JPL#82 Patroclus-Menoetius source closure](https://www2.boulder.swri.edu/~buie/biblio/pub099.html). Checked 2026-09-08. The full axes are halved once; the reference radius is the geometric mean of these semiaxes. This is the approximation's rendering scale, not an independent observed radius or the volume of the original convex reconstruction. Formal axis uncertainties are included only where the source supplies them.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: This review did not locate or qualify reusable imagery registered to the selected primary-component ellipsoid. Disk-integrated data and DAMIT model metadata are not surface maps.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Lucy mission and model references
entries.finding: The 2025 Lucy mission summary remains a contextual cross-reference. This metadata review did not use it to newly qualify the 127 × 117 × 98 km primary ellipsoid, a surface product, or physical mutual-event phase.

entries.subject: DAMIT model catalogue coverage
entries.finding: The cached 2026-09-13 official DAMIT asteroid/model/reference CSV exports were joined by exact asteroid name and contained no Patroclus row with a listed model. This is bounded DAMIT coverage, not evidence that no numerical model or revised binary solution exists elsewhere.
entries.revisitWhen: A future DAMIT export lists Patroclus, or a numerical primary-component release documents frame, scale and terms for comparison with the selected ellipsoid.
